title: PMCPA L2 canonical case
description: One corrected case object per CASE (multi-case reports contribute several). Every key is present on every record; absence is a value (null = genuinely absent or unresolved, "" = present but empty, [] = parsed and found nothing). Every canonical value carries its basis and the L1 slot values it beat. From l2.1, verdicts and segments are FILLED: an empty verdicts list now means a case whose outcome slots state nothing (outwith-scope and the no-report stubs), not an unfinished phase.

basis.description: A key of build.py's RULES registry, or an adjudication id. Membership is checked by validate.py, which holds the registry; the schema only fixes the shape.

segment_ref.description: A pointer into L1 pane text (pane summary|report, file = the L1 record's file) or into a substituted PDF flow (pane flow, file = the pdf_records file). text_length and text_sha256 describe the exact slice, so a consumer detects a changed L1 underneath instead of quoting the wrong span. Never partly null: a segment that does not exist is simply not emitted.

case_number.description: C1. ONE canonical case number. The filename is authoritative for which cases exist; the display form prefers info/meta where they agree, the h1 otherwise.

source_files.description: Never more than one: multi-case reports SHARE a file, they do not have several.

sibling_cases.description: Co-reported cases, canonical order. Siblings share report text, so bench must always assign them to the same split.

subject.description: C4. The hero h2 beats cludo:description. Semantic flips are recorded, not detected -- see build.py.

complainant.description: C7, PROSE-FIRST from l2.3 (DEFECTS D5 / the T1 blocker). Verbatim always retained; category is the SPEC §4 controlled vocabulary. Each of category / anonymous / contactable is resolved separately from the case report's own opening paragraph, with the one-word meta slot as fallback; `field_basis` names the rule that decided each and `sources` keeps every displaced value plus the sentence fragment the prose verdict was read from.

category.description: SPEC §4 controlled vocabulary. l2.4 removed `anonymous`: anonymity is not a role, it is the `anonymous` boolean below, and a case whose only stated fact was anonymity used to claim a category it never stated (audit fix 3d). The KEY set is unchanged.

anonymous.description: l2.4 (audit fix 1), tri-state. True = a statement of anonymity ('an anonymous complainant', 'wished to remain anonymous', or the meta/h1 token 'Anonymous'). False = a statement of NAMING ('a named, contactable complainant', or a complainant slot naming companies the corpus knows as respondents). null = neither was stated -- silence is never read as 'not anonymous', which is what the pre-l2.4 rule did on every case whose site metadata is the bare word 'Complainant'.

contactable.description: l2.3: read from the report opening ('an anonymous, non-contactable complainant'). null = neither the opening nor the summary states it (SPEC §6c) -- never a default.

meta_anonymous.description: the meta complainant slot or the h1 carries the word 'Anonymous'.

meta_named.description: l2.4: the meta complainant slot names companies the corpus knows as respondents (an inter-company complaint) or states the complainant was named ('Named, contactable complainant v CSL Vifor'). A role token names nobody and does not set this.

prose_source.description: The bounded prose pane used for complainant metadata. The `+explicit_anonymity_request` suffix records the reviewed full-report exception for an explicit first-person request that the complainant's name remain anonymous.

prose_named.description: l2.4: the report opening states the complainant was named ('a named, contactable complainant'). Positive evidence against anonymity; null where unstated.

prose_quotes.description: The sentence fragment each prose verdict was read from; null where that field was not stated. All five keys always present (SPEC §7.1 one key signature). `contactable` quotes the statement that DECIDED the field and `contactable_superseded` the earlier statement it overrode, so a case that states contactability twice shows both (l2.4, audit fix 2).

prose_category_frame.description: Wave C. Which frame read the role: `self_description` (the reflexive/stated-role/pen-name/prepositional frames -- the complainant's own words) or `narrator_subject` (the report's own opening sentence naming the complainant's role as the subject of the complaint verb). Null where no frame read one. The per-field `basis` names the same distinction.

field_basis.description: The rule that decided each field. Every value is a registered rule id.

code_year.description: C5. null with basis unresolved_pending_code_dates where no year is stated; inference from the received date needs data/code/.

dates.description: C10. ISO-8601; both source slots kept.

report_trailer_parsed.description: R12. The date the report's own trailer line states, parsed to ISO by the same rules as the info-holder slot, or null where the trailer states none. Recorded on every case so the comparison that produced `basis` is auditable, including where the trailer agrees.

verdicts.description: SPEC §5 / C11-C12. Ordinarily, one row per (clause, code_year, occurrence) the case's own outcome slots state a polarity for. The sole row-creating exception is the finite, full-report-hash-pinned PROSE_ONLY_VERDICT_READ audit (`basis = verdict_prose_only_reviewed`); unreviewed ruling prose still only attributes an existing row. [] is legitimate: outwith-scope cases and the no-report stubs state no outcome, and absence is a value. The outcome table and banner headings are cross-checks, never row-creating.

clause.description: One or two dotted components ('2', '9.1'). The Code has never had a three-level clause number.

code_year.description: From the clause chip's href where the page renders chips (2014+), else the outcome table's '(YYYY Code)' scope where it is the only year evidence, else the case's own code_year. THE ONLY place a null code_year is allowed to propagate: 57 cases state no Code year anywhere (C5, pending data/code/), and keying their clauses against an invented year would be worse than keying them against the null the source actually offers.

code_year_basis.description: R20. Which evidence level decided `code_year`: `year_uncontested` where the chip, the outcome-table '(YYYY Code)' scope and the case slot state at most one year between them; `year_clause_prose` / `year_case_prose` / `year_case_slot` where they disagreed and the report's own words, or failing that the case slot, settled it; `year_undecided_*` where nothing did; `year_prose_only_reviewed` for the finite hash-pinned rows whose clause is absent from every structured outcome slot; or an ADJUDICATION ID where a reviewed row in l2/adjudications.json (`verdicts[<clause>].code_year`, R20's residue round) read the report and keyed this row over witnesses that agreed. A null code_year is a REFUSAL under every basis EXCEPT `year_uncontested` -- the 57 cases that state no Code year anywhere carry null under that one.

occurrence.description: Disambiguates a clause ruled more than once in one case. Always 0 in l2.1: the corpus states multiplicity ('(xN)' on 584 outcome-table rows) but never separates the materials, so splitting would emit indistinguishable rows. The stated count is kept in sources.stated_multiplicity.

clause_slug.description: From the chip href. null before the chip era.

panel.description: The PANEL's ruling on this clause, and nothing else. l2.2 (DEFECTS D3): read ONLY from this case's panel_ruling prose on an appealed case, because the outcome lists state the post-appeal position and orienting them by who appealed put the Appeal Board's outcome here on 75+ items. On an UNAPPEALED case it is the stated polarity, which is not an inference: no other body ruled. null = attribution not established, never 'no ruling'.

appeal_board.description: The APPEAL BOARD's ruling on this clause, read only from this case's appeal-side prose (its ruling section and the appellant's grounds) and only where that prose names the Board as the body ruling. null = the Board did not demonstrably rule on this clause.

final.description: Never null: a row exists only where some source states a polarity.

dual_ruling.description: l2.2. This clause cannot be reduced to ONE Panel ruling: either the Panel's own prose states both polarities (several materials in one case) or both outcome lists name it on a case with no appeal. `final` still records that the clause was ruled on, and `panel` is null; bench/generate.py excludes these rows from every binary task rather than picking a side.

dual_ruling_appeal_board.description: R28 stage 1. The same statement about the APPEAL BOARD: it ruled this clause both ways, in different regards, so `appeal_board` is null and no single panel->board transition exists for T3. Kept apart from `dual_ruling` on purpose -- the Panel's own ruling on the clause may be perfectly single, and folding the two axes into one flag would delete correctly-labelled T1/T1-triage items. Every row carrying it was READ (l2/build.py DUAL_READ), not pattern-decided.

flipped_on_appeal.description: appealed AND panel AND appeal_board AND they differ -- both sides prose-derived, so a flip is a flip the report states, not a difference between two outcome lists.

sources.description: What each location said about THIS clause.

clause_code_year_prose.description: R20 receipt: {year: quote} for every Code year the report attaches to THIS clause ('Clause 9.1 of the 2016 Code'). Two entries means the clause was ruled under two editions in one case, which is a refusal, not a tie.

case_code_year_prose_decisive.description: R20 receipt: {year: quote} for every edition the report states for the CASE in a decisive frame ('considered under the 2019 Code', 'The outcome under the 2021 Code was', 'a breach of the 2016 Code was ruled').

case_code_year_prose_weak.description: R20 receipt: {year: quote} for the weaker edition frames ('the requirements of the 2006 Code applied'). Recorded, never used to decide: AUTH/2220/3/09 states one edition weakly and the other decisively, and its decisive one is the correct tag.

prose_appeal_from_grounds.description: The Appeal Board attribution rests on the appellant's grounds section rather than the Board's own ruling section. Those segments restate the PANEL's rulings constantly, so rows carrying this are the ones to sample first.

shared_report_evidence.description: true on a multi-case report: the info-holder, the meta CSVs and the outcome table belong to the page, not to a case within it, so every sibling claims the row.

rulings.description: R28 stage 1. One entry per prose ruling the build ATTRIBUTED to a body for this clause, in pane order, each with the ruling sentence verbatim and its offsets in the pane it was read from. A single ruling gets a one-entry list -- uniformity beats special-casing, and `len(rulings) > 1` is then the per-regard fact the scalars cannot carry. [] where no prose ruling was attributed (the outcome lists alone made the row). NOT here, and R27's measured limit rather than an oversight: rulings on clauses no outcome list names, since prose attributes a row and never creates one.

body.description: Which body ruled. Attribution is the same one-directional rule the scalars use: panel_ruling prose speaks only for the Panel, appeal-side prose only for the Board.

regard.description: The report's own MATTER heading covering this ruling, verbatim, or null where the report names no matter (single-matter reports, and the 13 PDF substitutions whose flow carries no sections). Never composed: see l2/build.py matter_headings.

regard_ref.description: Where the regard was cut from, so it can be re-sliced. null exactly when regard is null.

quote.description: The ruling sentence, verbatim from the pane. The receipt: l2/validate.py re-slices it at the offsets and reads it independently.

segment_kind.description: The segment kind the sentence was read from, which is what supplied the default speaker. null for a ruling supplied by the DUAL_READ registry (a half no frame can read).

source_frame.description: Which reader frame attributed it -- passive / active / uphold / coordinated / passive_that_clause / active_that_clause / not_warranted -- or `dual_read_registry` for a reviewed reading. Frames are tried in a fixed order and the first to read a (polarity, clause) owns it.

attribution_basis.description: Q3 / DEFECTS R6 + R28 stage-2. The adjudication id of a reviewed decision about WHICH BODY ruled what on this row (`verdicts[<clause>].attribution`), or null where no such decision applies -- which is every row but ten. It is kept apart from `basis` on purpose: three of the ten are panel-axis duals the RULE decided, and `check_dual_read_coverage` reads `basis` to exempt a rule-decided dual, so overwriting it made the build refuse rows that were already read. A row can therefore say both which rule produced it and which reading corrected an attribution on it.

appeal.description: C6. `by` is 'none' where the source states there was no appeal, and null where it states nothing -- the 64 pages with both slots empty stay unresolved rather than being folded to 'none' on no evidence.

report_appeal_headings.description: R18. The report's own 'APPEAL BY <party>' / 'APPEAL FROM <party>' section headings, verbatim, in document order. [] where the report carries none -- parsed and found nothing, not 'not recorded'. A third witness to `by`, independent of the two PMCPA slots, which are both false on AUTH/3028/3/18 and AUTH/3535/7/21.

additional.description: From the rendered chips, deduplicated in stated order; the raw chip list is in sources.

clause_2_censure.description: Any verdict row for a bare clause 2 whose final is breach.

segments.description: SPEC §6. Canonical narrative structure, in fixed emission order: the abstract, then the body sections in char order (kinds legitimately REPEAT -- a multi-case report runs COMPLAINT/RESPONSE/PANEL RULING once per case), then the renditions. Siblings share the list: the report is one document. [] is legitimate for the no-report stubs.

leakage_attest.description: SPEC §6 (six checks since 2026-08-10: `no_outcome_heading` is DEFECTS R26 -- the publisher's outcome-stating HEADLINE above the first body section, which l1/derive's three literal banner strings miss). Recomputed by validate.py on the re-sliced text with its own READING of each check -- not a copy of the builder's regex, which is how R24's decimal-point hole survived in two witnesses at once; the builder is never its own witness. complaint/response are the only kinds bench T1/T2 may quote, and a failing attest means the item is not generated, never trimmed by hand. Note that `clean` is structurally false for the abstract and abstract_rendition kinds: both lie inside the measured abstract, so outside_abstract cannot pass for them. Read the individual checks for those two.

renditions.description: The paraphrase inventory for bench P1: INDICES into segments[], not bare refs, because a rendition is a segment and carries its own attest. summary and report_abstract point at the LEADING allegation span of each account, cut before the first ruling language; pdf_flow points at the substituted PDF's abstract segment. null = no such span exists (under 200 chars, or the account itself is absent).

entities.description: Redaction and contamination support. products and people_roles are still [] and that is NOT a parsed-and-found-nothing claim: the extractor has not run (SPEC §10.4 is open on whether people_roles is worth extracting before a benchmark needs it).

multi_case_undeclared.description: l2.2 (DEFECTS D4). The report pane carries a case-report banner for a case this page does not declare as a sibling, so segments mix parties and the page-level outcome lists cover more than this case. Recorded, never repaired -- attributing rulings per case inside a shared pane is out of scope -- and bench excludes the case's items.

multi_case_banners.description: The foreign case numbers whose banners were found. [] when there are none.

known_text_defects.description: Not yet populated -- the ligature-loss and glyph audits live in the PDF layer and have not been folded up.
